If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in the last 2 days, shift forecast downward by 1–2% for late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect reversal risk.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows upward trend, reduce slope by 0.1–0.3% per day for early horizon to dampen momentum.

If sentiment is mixed and forecast shows downward trend, increase slope by 0.1–0.3% per day for mid horizon to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment is high in last 5 days and forecast is flat, introduce 0.5–1.0% upward bias for late horizon to capture breakout potential.
